title: Adic line-system comparison through cofinal indices and rational coefficient colimits
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to a larger sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with finite limits, and $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor preserving finite limits and coverings. Let $L$ be its geometric inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed poset whose underlying set belongs to the sheaf universe. For each $i\in I$ let $(R_{i,m})_{m\ge1}$ and $(S_{i,m})_{m\ge1}$ be inverse towers of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$. Write $R_i=\varprojlim_mR_{i,m}$ and $S_i=\varprojlim_mS_{i,m}$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Assume compatible ring isomorphisms $a_{i,m}:LR_{i,m}\cong S_{i,m}$ and a ring isomorphism $a_i:LR_i\cong S_i$ whose $m$-th projection is $a_{i,m}L(\mathrm{pr}_m)$.
Choose integers $e_i\ge1$ and put $B_{i,n}=R_{i,e_in}$, $B'_{i,n}=S_{i,e_in}$. Let $(M_{i,n})_n$ be a tower of $B_{i,n}$-module sheaves and $(N_{i,n})_n$ a tower of $B'_{i,n}$-module sheaves, with semilinear transitions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume compatible isomorphisms $c_{i,n}:LM_{i,n}\cong N_{i,n}$ semilinear over $a_{i,e_in}$. For each $i$ assume one covering $\{V_{ij}\to1_{\mathcal C}\}_j$ and compatible bases $b_{ij,n}:B_{i,n}|_{V_{ij}}\cong M_{i,n}|_{V_{ij}}$, with $t_nb_{ij,n+1}=b_{ij,n}\rho_n$, on the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Put $M_i=\varprojlim_nM_{i,n}$, $N_i=\varprojlim_nN_{i,n}$, with scalar actions via $R_i,S_i$ and their subsequence projections.
Assume also specified directed diagrams in $i$ of the pairs $(B_{i,n},M_{i,n})$ and $(B'_{i,n},N_{i,n})$ for every $n$, with ring homomorphisms and semilinear module maps commuting with the tower transitions, $a$ and $c$. Their induced limit diagrams are required to use the corresponding ring maps $R_i\to R_j$, $S_i\to S_j$. Let $s_i\in R_i(1_{\mathcal C})$ be compatible global sections, and let $s'_i=a_i(Ls_i)$. For a module $M$ over $R$ write $M[1/s]$ for the sheafified sequential colimit $M\xrightarrow{s}M\xrightarrow{s}\cdots$, with its canonical action of the likewise localized ring $R[1/s]$; equivalently this is $M\otimes_RR[1/s]$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then the projection equations
$$\mathrm{pr}_n\theta_i=c_{i,n}L(\mathrm{pr}_n)$$
define isomorphisms $\theta_i:LM_i\cong N_i$ semilinear over $a_i$, independent of the bases and natural in all the specified tower maps. They extend uniquely along the localization cocones to compatible isomorphisms
$$LM_i[1/s_i]\cong N_i[1/s'_i].$$
Here $LM_i[1/s_i]$ means $L(M_i[1/s_i])$. On the sheafified filtered colimits in $i$ they induce an isomorphism
$$L\bigl(\varinjlim_iM_i[1/s_i]\bigr)\cong\varinjlim_iN_i[1/s'_i],$$
semilinear over $L(\varinjlim_iR_i[1/s_i])\cong\varinjlim_iS_i[1/s'_i]$. The scalar action on each filtered colimit is the sheafification of $[r_i][m_j]=[r_km_k]$ at any common upper bound $k\ge i,j$. All comparisons are fixed by the displayed projections, localization maps and colimit coprojections. Restricting a compatible sequence to $m=e_in$ identifies the full coefficient limits with these subsequence limits; the inverse takes its $m$-th coordinate by reducing any coordinate at $e_in\ge m$.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and abbreviate $e=e_i$. For any sectionwise coefficient tower $T_m$, restriction sends $(x_m)_m$ to $(x_{en})_n$. Conversely, given a compatible subsequence $(y_n)_n$, define $x_m$ by applying the transition $T_{en}\to T_m$ to $y_n$ for any $en\ge m$. Such $n$ exists since $e\ge1$. Two choices give the same answer by comparison at a larger subsequence index. For $m'\ge m$ reduction sends $x_{m'}$ to $x_m$; the two constructions are inverse. They commute with restriction of sections, ring operations, tower maps and every subsequence projection. Thus $R_i\cong\varprojlim_nB_{i,n}$ and $S_i\cong\varprojlim_nB'_{i,n}$ as ring sheaves, with precisely the stated projections.

proof.text: Let $B_n=B_{i,n}$. The maps $a_{i,en}$ identify the tower $LB_n$ with $B'_{i,n}$. They induce an isomorphism $A:\varprojlim_nLB_n\to\varprojlim_nB'_{i,n}$: apply $a_{i,en}$ coordinatewise, with inverse given by their inverses. Let $\kappa:L(\varprojlim_nB_n)\to\varprojlim_nLB_n$ be the projection-induced comparison. Using step 1 to identify its source with $LR_i$ and the target of $A$ with $S_i$, the $n$-th projection of $A\kappa$ is $a_{i,en}L(\mathrm{pr}_{en})$, which is the $en$-th projection of $a_i$ by hypothesis. Coordinate projections determine a map into a limit, so $A\kappa=a_i$. Hence $\kappa$ is an isomorphism. This uses the assumed comparison $a_i$, without claiming that $L$ preserves arbitrary inverse limits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-inverse-image-compatible-free-tower] to $B_n$, $M_{i,n}$ and $L$. Its coefficient-limit hypothesis is $\kappa$ from step 2. The sites, universes and finite-limit/cover preservation are those of the item. Its single common cover and transition-compatible bases are exactly the given $V_{ij}$ and $b_{ij,n}$; no separate choice of a cover for each $n$ is used. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\delta_i:LM_i\to\varprojlim_nLM_{i,n}$, linear over $\kappa$. Coordinatewise application of $c_{i,n}$ gives an isomorphism $C_i:\varprojlim_nLM_{i,n}\to N_i$; compatibility with transitions makes both this map and its coordinatewise inverse well-defined. Put $\theta_i=C_i\delta_i$. Its $n$-th projection is $c_{i,n}L(\mathrm{pr}_n)$.

proof.text: The semilinearity equations for the $c_{i,n}$ show in coordinate $n$ that $\theta_i(rm)$ equals the product of the $en$-th projection of $a_i(r)$ with the $n$-th projection of $\theta_i(m)$. Thus $\theta_i$ is semilinear over $a_i$. For a specified tower map $v:M_{i,\bullet}\to M_{j,\bullet}$ with target map $v'$, project $\theta_jL(v)$ and $v'\theta_i$ to level $n$. The two resulting maps are $c_{j,n}L(v_n\mathrm{pr}_n)$ and $v'_nc_{i,n}L(\mathrm{pr}_n)$; these agree by the assumed square for $c$. Hence the two limit maps agree. The same projection argument treats any compatible semilinear tower map and shows uniqueness of $\theta_i$. Since its defining projections mention no bases, it is independent of the cover and bases.

source.place: The integral twist and Rational and algebraic closure paragraphs: normalization and naturality on every projection

proof.text: For any ring sheaf $R$, global section $s$, and $R$-module sheaf $M$, form the presheaf $P(U)=\varinjlim_{q\ge0}(M(U)\xrightarrow{s}M(U)\to\cdots)$. Presheaf module colimits are sectionwise and their underlying abelian presheaves are the abelian colimits [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-modules-colimits-sectionwise]. The module-localization colimit lemma therefore identifies it with $M(U)[1/s]$, taking stage $q$ to $m/s^q$. The maps commute with restriction, so this is a presheaf identification. The sheafification of $P$ is the colimit in abelian sheaves: maps from it to a sheaf are, by the two universal properties, exactly compatible families of maps from the sequential diagram. The presheaf $T(U)=R(U)[1/s]$ acts by $(r/s^p)(m/s^q)=rm/s^{p+q}$; module sheafification over a presheaf ring gives the action of $T^\#$ on $P^\#$. By definition $T^\#$ is the sheafified localization $R[1/s]$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], with its canonical map from $R$. Thus the sequential definition in the item has the actual localized-ring action. Multiplication by $s$ in the sequential diagram is only a module map; the ring $T$ is the fraction ring, not a colimit of ring maps $R\xrightarrow{s}R$.

For completeness the tensor description agrees with this sequential model. At $U$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] gives $M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}T(U)\cong P(U)$, with $m\otimes r/s^q\mapsto rm/s^q$ (using the symmetry of tensor). These identifications commute with restriction by that formula. Sheafification of presheaf tensor products is the tensor product of the module sheafifications, by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor]. Since $M$ and $R$ are already sheaves, this identifies $P^\#$ with $M\otimes_RR[1/s]$ and identifies $m/1$ with $m\otimes1$. In particular it is the localization specified in the statement, with the same cocone maps.

The geometric inverse image $L$ preserves finite limits and all colimits [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence] applies to $R_i$, $s_i$ and $M_i$; by step 6, $M_i[1/s_i]=R_i[1/s_i]\otimes_{R_i}M_i$ is its localization. It gives ring and module isomorphisms $L(R_i[1/s_i])\cong(LR_i)[1/Ls_i]$ and $L(M_i[1/s_i])\cong(LM_i)[1/Ls_i]$, preserving the localization units and compatible with the specified ring isomorphism $a_i:LR_i\cong S_i$, which sends $Ls_i$ to $s'_i$; so $a_i$ yields $L(R_i[1/s_i])\cong S_i[1/s'_i]$. By step 4, $\theta_i$ is $a_i$-semilinear, so it carries multiplication by $Ls_i$ to multiplication by $s'_i$ and is an isomorphism of the sequential diagrams $LM_i\xrightarrow{Ls_i}LM_i\to\cdots$ and $N_i\xrightarrow{s'_i}N_i\to\cdots$. By step 5 (on $\mathcal D$) it induces $(LM_i)[1/Ls_i]\cong N_i[1/s'_i]$, with inverse induced by $\theta_i^{-1}$. It is semilinear: filtered colimits of sets commute with finite products, set sheafification preserves them, and algebraic sheafification has the underlying set sheafification, so it suffices to test pairs of representatives at stages $p,q$, where the equation is $\theta_i(rm)=a_i(r)\theta_i(m)$. All maps are fixed on each localization coprojection, which gives uniqueness. For a specified map over $R_i\to R_j$, compatibility of the $s_i$ makes it a map of these sequential diagrams, and both composites agree on every coprojection by step 4; so naturality persists after localization.

source.place: Rational and algebraic closure paragraph: inverse image commutes with colimits and scalar multiplication

proof.text: Write $T_i(U)=R_i(U)[1/s_i]$ and $P_i(U)=M_i(U)[1/s_i]$. First take both $T(U)=\varinjlim_iT_i(U)$ and $P(U)=\varinjlim_iP_i(U)$ as abelian groups. On $T(U)$ define $[r_i][t_j]=[r_kt_k]$ at a common upper bound $k$, with unit $[1]$. The representative criterion makes this well-defined; the ring identities hold at a common stage. A compatible family of ring maps extends uniquely to an additive map from $T(U)$ and respects this multiplication on representatives, so $T(U)$ is the ring colimit as well. Every group element has a stage representative, and equality of two representatives holds at a common later stage, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] with base ring $\mathbf Z$; ring equalities have the same criterion by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero]. Define $[r_i][m_j]=[r_km_k]$ at $k\ge i,j$. Two choices of $k$ agree after passage to a common upper bound, by semilinearity of the transitions. Changing representatives also gives equality after an upper bound of the stages witnessing both equalities. All module identities are checked at a common stage for the finitely many entries, where they are the module identities of $P_k(U)$ over $T_k(U)$. Restrictions preserve this formula. Thus $P$ is a presheaf of modules over the commutative ring presheaf $T$. The same construction applies to $S_i,N_i$.

source.place: Tags 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit) and 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit), with the displayed common-upper-bound scalar formula

proof.text: Sheafifying the presheaves in step 8 gives the asserted filtered colimits. Indeed presheaf colimits are sectionwise and sheafification is left adjoint, so maps from $P^\#$ to an abelian sheaf are compatible families of maps from $P_i$ to it. Each such map extends uniquely across $P_i\to P_i^\#$, giving precisely the filtered-colimit universal property for the localized module sheaves of step 5; the same argument in rings treats $T^\#$. The presheaf-ring module-sheafification interface extends the action to $T^\#\times P^\#\to P^\#$ and fixes its normalization. To test equality of action maps it suffices to test pairs of stage representatives: filtered colimits of sets commute with finite products, sheafification preserves finite products, and the underlying set of abelian/ring sheafification is set sheafification. Consequently the sheaf product of these colimits is the sheafified colimit of the products at a common stage. This also explains why the formula in the statement is a sheafification formula, rather than an assertion that every global section has a single global representative.

Finally apply colimit preservation of $L$ to the $i$-diagram of localized modules and then take the colimit of the compatible isomorphisms of step 7. This gives $L(\varinjlim_iM_i[1/s_i])\cong\varinjlim_iN_i[1/s'_i]$. Taking the same construction for the ring diagrams gives $L(\varinjlim_iR_i[1/s_i])\cong\varinjlim_iS_i[1/s'_i]$. The ring and module comparisons commute with every coprojection. To check multiplicativity or semilinearity, use the stage-product test proved in step 9 and finite-product preservation of $L$. On a common stage the requisite equation is respectively the ring equation or the action equation of step 7; hence it holds on the full colimits. Their inverses are the colimits of the inverse comparisons, so the resulting maps are isomorphisms with the stated scalar action. Projection uniqueness (steps 2–4), localization-cocone uniqueness (step 7), and the colimit universal property fix all the comparisons and their compatibility.
